MESSAGE FROM THE PRESIDENT OF GOVERNING BODY
                       It gives me great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to all the aspiring students
                       seeking admission to our esteemed institution. At PDUAM Dalgaon, we believe in
                       providing a transformative education that empowers students to excel in their
                       chosen fields and make a positive impact in society. Our college is dedicated to
                       fostering a holistic learning environment that nurtures intellectual curiosity, critical
                       thinking, and a passion for scientific inquiry.

Our dedicated faculty members, with their wealth of knowledge and expertise, are committed to providing
you with a comprehensive and engaging learning experience. Alongside a rigorous academic curriculum, we
also emphasize the development of essential life skills, character building, and a deep-rooted sense of social
responsibility.
I extend my heartfelt welcome to all new students seeking admission to PDUAM Dalgaon. Together, let us
embark on a transformative academic journey filled with knowledge, growth, and endless possibilities.
Regards,
Dr. Sachindra Sahariah
Retd. Assoc Prof. Mangaldai college & President GB, PDUAM Dalgaon


MESSAGE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

                       PDUAM Dalgaon is a distinguished institution dedicated to providing a holistic
                       education in the field of science. As the Principal, it is my honor to extend a heartfelt
                       welcome to all prospective students seeking admission to our esteemed college.

                       PDUAM Dalgaon, established by the Government of Assam, is a model degree
                       college that epitomizes excellence in education. Our college offers comprehensive
                       Higher
Secondary (12th) Course in Science under the esteemed AHSEC, Guwahati. We are also thrilled to announce
that we will be introducing a transformative Four-Year Undergraduate Programme in both Arts and Science
stream under the esteemed Gauhati University (GU-FYUGP), in alignment with the progressive National
Education Policy 2020 of India.
At PDUAM Dalgaon, we believe in fostering an environment that nurtures intellectual growth, creativity, and
critical thinking. Our dedicated faculty members, who are experts in their respective fields, strive to provide
quality education and mentorship, empowering students to reach their fullest potential.
Beyond academics, we offer a lively campus life, where students can engage in a wide range of co-curricular
activities, including sports, cultural events, and community service initiatives. We believe in holistic
development, encouraging students to explore their passions and develop essential life skills that will shape
their future endeavours.
We look forward to welcoming you to our college, where you will be surrounded by a community of
motivated learners and dedicated educators. Together, we will create a future where your aspirations
become a reality.
Regards
Dr. Lakhi Prasad Hazarika
Principal, PDUAM Dalgaon
 THE COLLEGE AT A GLANCE

Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Adarsha Mahavidyalaya, Dalgaon is established as Govt. Model Colleges
(General) under the primary components of Rashtriya Uchchattar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA). RUSA (Hindi for
“National Higher Education Mission”) is a holistic scheme of development for higher education in India
initiated in 2013 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Government of India.

Location

The college is 500 meters away from National Highway No. 15 and is about 2 kms away from Dalgaon town.
It is located at the conjunction of two places, Kharupetia and Bechimari at longitude 92.1928060 and latitude
26.5460190, both of which have busy commercial sectors. The Dalgaon Police station, the Dalgaon Circle
office and the Dalgaon Health Centre are also in proximity of the college.

Connectivity

The college is well-connected to the other parts of the town. Buses coming from and going to locations as
far as Tezpur and Guwahati on the highway all day long. Local public vehicles like the E -rickshaw, Auto
rickshaw and passenger vans are always available. The Rowta Railway Station, Udalguri is located at 24 kms
away from the college

VISION, MISSION & GOALS

Vision

To provide equity and quality education to the educationally, socially, economically weaker section of the
society.

Mission

   ❖ To prepare young minds to be productive members of their community, society, and country at large.
   ❖ To provide access to higher education to the disadvantaged sections of the society, especially the
     educationally backward sections and the persons with disability.
   ❖ To train the students to develop Professionalism, Humanism and Social Responsibility.
   ❖ To encourage scientific inquisitiveness for constructive social transformation.
   ❖ To accelerate the inclusion of female students, and the persons with disabilities in higher education.
   ❖ To promote collaboration with industries and other organizations for research and add on courses
     for the students for skill development and enriching academics

Goals

   ❖ Facilitating a learning environment conductive to holistic development of students.
   ❖ Igniting scientific temper among the students in order to reorient attitudes and prejudices.
   ❖ Nurturing students with employability skills.
   ❖ To act as a catalyst of change by spreading science education and by strengthening the people of its
     vicinity.
   ❖ To inculcate values of discipline, perseverance, team spirit and to enhance critical abilities in
     students.
 NAAC ACCREDITATION

The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) Peer Team conducted a comprehensive
evaluation visit to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Adarsha Mahavidyalaya (PDUAM) Dalgaon on May 8th and
9th, 2024. The team comprised esteemed academicians, namely Prof. J Singh Khattar, Prof. R Ramteke, and
Dr. S P Saraswat, serving as the Chairperson, Member Coordinator, and Member respectively.

During the evaluation visit, the NAAC Peer Team meticulously examined various aspects of PDUAM Dalgaon’s
academic and administrative functioning. They conducted interviews with faculty, staff, students and
guardians, scrutinized documents, observed infrastructure facilities, and assessed the quality of teaching,
research, and extension activities.

After a thorough evaluation, the NAAC accredited PDUAM Dalgaon with a CGPA of 2.51 on a seven point
scale at B+ Grade valid for a period of 5 Years from May 16, 2024. This accreditation reflects the institution’s
commitment to maintaining high standards of quality in education and overall academic excellence.

FACILITIES AVAILABLE

National Service Scheme

The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of the college is very active and has been continuously providing its
service to the society. NSS is an Govt. of India sponsored public service program conducted by the
Department of Youth Affairs and Sports of the Government of India. NSS is a voluntary association of young
people in Colleges, Universities and at +2 level working for a campus community linkage. The philosophy of
the NSS underlines the belief that the welfare of an individual is ultimately dependent on the welfare of the
society on the whole and therefore, the NSS volunteers shall strive for the well-being of the society.

Mentor-Mentee Forum

There shall be separate Mentor-Mentee Forum semester-wise, department-wise and student-wise
comprising the mentor to be appointed by concerned HoD and the assigned mentees which shall be
responsible for transaction of curriculum and performing all other activities for the assigned mentees in
which the concerned mentor shall act as Chairperson and a nominated/selected mentee as Coordinator. It
is like the ‘Quality Circle’ with the overall goal of improving the teaching learning process.

Science Laboratories

The five major departments of the college, namely Botany, Chemistry, Computer Science, Physics and
Zoology have five well-equipped laboratories furnished with modern equipment. These are large enough to
accommodate a class of 30-40 students at one time for conducting practicals. Practical examinations are also
conducted at the college as per the permission and guidelines of Gauhati University and AHSEC, Guwahati.

Computer Centre

The college has a Computer Centre fully equipped with 20 nos. of Intel 7th Generation Core i3 (7100)
desktops and latest software with an environment to implement and experiment knowledge acquired in the
classroom. All the systems are connected to BSNL fibre/ JIO Airfiber broadband internet facility.
 Library

The central library of the college offers a spacious and comfortable reading area that welcomes both
students and faculty. With over 3,600 textbooks and reference books lining the shelves—and new titles being
added regularly—the library serves as a rich academic resource. The central library also maintains a digital
institutional repository to support academic and research activities. To keep our readers informed and
updated, the library subscribes to two daily newspapers and seven magazines/periodicals covering a range
of topics. Additionally, users have access to e-books and academic journals through INFLIBNET’s ONOS
(Online Access to E-Resources) service, ensuring seamless learning and research opportunities.


Smart Classrooms

There are four smart classrooms equipped with digital interactive panels, projectors, audio systems and an
active internet facility which provide advanced teaching-learning processes and mechanisms.

Open Air Stage

The college has an open-air stage meant for organizing cultural, annual, and other programs. It has the
capacity to accommodate around 500 spectators comfortably at a time.

Sports and Gymnasium

The college has a volleyball court and a football ground where the students spend their recreational hours
playing. Besides, there are such indoor games facilities as chess, carrom and table tennis. Sports gears for all
the sports are also available. The playground also has a cricket pitch where students and teachers like to play
after college hours. The gymnasium consists of treadmills and other gym equipment. The college football
team has successfully participated in District level events organized by District Administration, Darang.

Conference Hall

The college has a conference hall with all the modern facilities that provides the right environment and
ambiance for various programmes, seminars, conferences and lectures.
Pure Drinking Water

The water purifier for pure drinking water is installed within the Academic block. During summer, fresh and
pure drinking water is provided to the students and staff through the Water Cooler.

Washroom Facility

The college has separate toilet blocks for college staff, girls and boys on each of its two floors with proper
running water.

Facilities for Differently Abled Students

The college provides special facilities for the mobility of differently abled students. Students with disabilities
are entitled to access all schemes, facilities and services in the college. There are ramps, rails and washrooms
for their benefit.
 Scholarships

There are provisions for the following Scholarships subject to fulfilment of eligibility criteria:

   ❖ National Merit scholarship
   ❖ State Merit Scholarship
   ❖ Post Matric Scholarship for SC/ST/OBC Students
   ❖ Scholarship for Physically Handicapped Students
   ❖ Merit cum means scholarship for the students of Minority Community
   ❖ Chief Minister Nijut Moina Scheme

Hostel

The college has a well-equipped, fully furnished girls’ hostel. It is secured with boundary walls on all sides
and is located within the college campus along with the teachers’ quarters. Application forms for hostel
admission can be collected from the college office and handed over to the appointed office attendant after
admission into the college. The list of selected boarders will be finalized by the college and hostel authorities
based on merit. No seat can be reserved prior to admission.

Boys’ Hostel is also under construction and about to complete by this year. Students can also find well -
furnished, homely, and affordable PGs near the campus as it is in a densely residential area.

FOUR YEAR UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMME (FYUGP) COURSE STRUCTURE
The Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) of PDUAM, Dalgaon under Gauhati University is as per
UGC’s Curricular Framework, published in November 2022. The course structure of FYUGP is built on the
Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS). In the FYUGP, one has choice to exit from the programme thrice – after
one year, after two years, and after three years. If one exits the programme after one year, one gets a
certificate. If one exits after two years, one gets a diploma. If one exits after three years, one gets a Bachelor’s
Degree. And finally, if a student completes the whole 4-year, one gets a Bachelor’s Degree (Honours).

If a student exits the FYUGP after 3 years, s/he will need to take admission into the first year of a Master’s
programme, which is a 2-year degree programme. However, if a student fully completes an FYUGP, s/he
needs to take admission into the second year of a Master’s programme and needs to complete only one year
to get a Master’s Degree. Under CBCS, there was no such pathways.
Once a student takes admission into a Master’s programme either after 3 years of the Bachelor’s programme
or after FYUGP, one will be able to take admission into a Doctoral programme leading to the Degree of PhD.
However, if a student is exceptionally good, one can directly take admission into a Doctoral programme right
after the FYUGP, bypassing the Master’s programme.
 FYUGP Progression




The progression and multiple exits during the whole course structure is given below.

After 1 Year
One can exit just after one-year. In this case, the student will have to complete one extra Vocational / Skill
course (Exit Course) of 4 credits and can exit the programme. The student will get a Certificate. The minimum
total credit requirement is 44 (and 4 credit extra for the exit Vocational course).

After 2 Years
One can exit the programme after two-year course as well. In this case, the student will have to complete
one extra Vocational / Skill course of 4 credits and can exit the programme. The student will get a Diploma.
The minimum total credit requirement is 88 (and 4 credits extra for the exit Vocational course).

After 3 Years
If a student completes 3 years, s/he can exit the programme. In this case the student will get a Bachelor’s
Degree. The minimum total credit requirements is 120.
After 4 Years
After completion of 4 years, the student gets either a Bachelor’s Degree (Honours) or a Bachelor’s Degree
(Honours) with Research. The minimum total credit requirements is 160. It should be noted that any
certificate / diploma / degree is awarded only if the student clears (i.e. passes) all the required courses
(papers) till that point of time.
N.B.: Every student who wants to exit before 3 years into the programme, MUST complete an additional
Vocational Course of 4 credits.
 COURSE STRUCTURE
The FYUGP is designed to offer Bachelor’s Degree to the students. The whole FYUGP is divided into two parts
– Core Courses and Common Courses. The minimum credit allocation for a 3-year programme is 84 credits
in core courses and 36 credits in common courses, which comes to a total of minimum 120 credits for a
three-year programme. A student can earn up to maximum of 132 credits in a 3 – year programme using
optional free credits of 12 (4+4+4).

There are two streams – (i) Arts and (ii) Science available at PDUAM Dalgaon and each stream has their own
subject groups as listed below.

   ❖ MIL: Assamese

   ❖ Other Language: English

   ❖ Physical Science: Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics
   ❖ Computer & Information Science: Computer Science

Common Courses at PDUAM Dalgaon
The common courses are to be studied by all students alike and all-together they carry a total credit of 36
over a 3-year period. These courses are further divided into five (5) subcategories, as described below

Multi-disciplinary Courses
Each student needs to take at any three papers, each with 3-credits from the following sub groups
       1.   Natural and Physical Science
       2.   Mathematical Sciences
       3.   Library, Information and Media Sciences
       4.   Humanities and Social Sciences
       5.   Information and Communication Technologies and
       6.   Life Sciences

The levels of these courses are of Class XII. Each student need to take all the three papers from one
Multidisciplinary Group

Value Added Course (VAC)
The VAC courses will come from following sub groups

       1. Environmental Science (Compulsory)
       2. Any one paper from following sub groups
          i.  Understanding India
         ii.  Digital and Technological Solutions

Each student will have to take any three courses, each of 2-credit, from any three groups during Semesters
1, 2, & 4. Here one course from the Environmental Science group is compulsory.

Skill Enhancement Course (SEC)
These are various skill courses with total credit allocation of 9. All students need to complete three skill
courses, each with 3 credits during Semesters 1-3.
 Ability Enhancement Courses (AEC)
This is an 8-credit course covering Modern Indian Languages (MIL)/Alternative English and English Usage
(Communication). Each student needs to complete two papers of 4-credits each – one from English Usage
and other from the group of MIL, especially designed for this purpose.

Internship
All student is to carry out an internship with a credit allocation of 4. The internship can be carried out in any
semester during Semesters 4 and 5. As internships are meant to be done during semester breaks, they will
not interfere with other classes.

The Fourth Year
In the FYUGP, the fourth year is at par with the first year of a Master’s programme, as a student can directly
take admission into the second year of a Master’s programme after the successful completion of the FYUGP.
In the fourth year, a student has to complete one compulsory paper on Research Methodology (REM) in the
Semester VII, which is a 4-credit theory paper. The rest of courses will consist of Advanced Core Courses and
a Dissertation.

ABC (Academic Bank of Credits)
 The GU-FYUGP is directly connected to the ABC (Academic Bank of Credit) as
 notified by the UGC. All credits a student earn at the end of an examination in
 GU-FYUGP, will be deposited in the ABC by the university. As such it is
 mandatory that a student under GU-FYUGP register for the ABC as notified by

 CURBING THE MENACE OF RAGGING IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS
It is brought to the notice of the Public that ragging is a criminal offence and that UGC has framed UGC
Regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009, in order to prohibit,
prevent and eliminate the scourge of ragging in Indian Universities/Colleges/Institutions.

The above regulations are mandatory and all Intuitions should take necessary steps for its implementation
under intimation to the UGC.

Students in distress owing to ragging related incidents can access the Toll Free Helpline 1800-180-5522 or
contact Ed. CIL (India) Limited, Ed. CIL House, 18A, Sector-16A, Noida-201 301, UP.

                                                                                    Sd/-
                                                                                 Secretary
                                                                 University Grants Commission, New Delhi


UGC REGULATIONS ON CURBING THE MENACE OF RAGGING IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS,
2009

In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (g) of Sub-Section (1) of Section 26 of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956, the University Grants Commission, hereby, makes the following Regulations, namely-
Title, commencement and applicability:

1. These regulations shall be called the "UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher
Educational Institutions, 2009".

2. They shall come into force with immediate effect.

3. They shall apply to all the Universities established or incorporated by or under a Central Act, a Provincial
Act or a State Act, to all Institutions deemed to be University under Section 3 of UGC Act, 1956, to all other
higher Educational Institutions, Including the departments, constituent units and all the premises (academic,
residential, sports, canteen, etc.) of such Universities, deemed University and other Higher Educational
Institutions, whether located within the campus or outside, and to all means of transportation of students
whether public or private.

Objective

To root out raging in all its forms from Universities, Colleges and other educational institutions in the country
by prohibiting it by law, preventing its occurrence by following the provision of these regulations and
punishing those who indulge in ragging as provided for in these regulations and the appropriate law in force.

"Ragging" means the following:

Any conduct whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or
handling with rudeness any other student, indulging in rowdy or undisciplined activities which causes or is
likely to cause annoyance, hardship or psychological harm or to raise rear or apprehension thereof in a
fresher or a junior student or asking the students to do any act or perform something which such student
will not in the ordinary course and which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame or
embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of a fresher or a junior student.
 Punishable ingredients or Ragging:

   ❖ Abetment to ragging;
   ❖ Criminal conspiracy to ragging;
   ❖ Unlawful assembly and rioting while ragging;
   ❖ Public nuisance created during ragging;
   ❖ Violation of decency and morals through ragging;
   ❖ Injury to body, causing hurt or grievous hurt;
   ❖ Wrongful restraint;
   ❖ Wrongful confinement;
   ❖ Use of criminal force;
   ❖ Assault as well as sexual offences or unnatural offences;
   ❖ Extortion;
   ❖ Criminal trespass;
   ❖ Offences against property;
   ❖ Criminal intimidation;
   ❖ Attempts to commit any or all of the above-mentioned offences against the victim (s);
   ❖ Physical or psychological humiliation;
   ❖ All other offences following from the definition of "Ragging".

Punishments At the institution level:

Depending upon the nature and gravity of the offence as established by the Anti-Ragging Committee of the
institution, the possible punishments for those found guilty of ragging at the institution level shall be any
one or any combination of the following:

   ❖ Suspension from attending classes and academic privileges.
   ❖ Withholding/Withdrawing scholarship/fellowship and other benefits.
   ❖ Debarring from appearing in any test/examination or other evaluation process.
   ❖ Withholding results.
   ❖ Debarring from representing the institution in any regional, National or International meet,
     tournament, Youth festival, etc.
   ❖ Suspension/ Expulsion from the hostel.
   ❖ Cancellation of Admission.
   ❖ Rustication from the Institution for a period ranging from 1 to 4 semesters.
   ❖ Expulsion from the Institution and consequent debarring from admission to any other institution for
     specified period.
   ❖ Fine ranging between Rupees 25,000/- and Rupees 1 Lakh.
   ❖ Collective punishment: when the persons committing or abetting the crime of ragging are not
     identified, the institution shall resort to collective punishment.
